chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadalah, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about the sacrificial animal that is garlanded or marked, then perishes. He said: If it was voluntary, then nothing else is due upon him; but if it was an expiation or a vow, then a replacement is due upon him.

key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: the sacrificial animal designated for offering in the rites of hajj
key_terms.تَطَوُّعًا: a voluntary offering not required by obligation
key_terms.جَزَاءً: an expiatory offering due as compensation
key_terms.نَذْرًا: an offering made obligatory by vow
key_terms.يُشْعَرُ: is marked as a sacrificial animal
key_terms.يُقَلَّدُ: is garlanded as a sign that it has been designated as sacrificial offering

ai.seo_question: If a designated sacrificial animal dies before reaching its place of sacrifice, must it be replaced?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a sacrificial animal designated for offering that dies before reaching its place of sacrifice. If the offering was voluntary, no substitute is required; but if it was obligatory due to expiation or vow, a replacement must be provided.
